author: raoatifshad
body:
**PR Description**

With this PR the IB test logs are scanned for problems while cms-bot is already reading them, so the IB chatbot no longer has to copy and unpack the zip files again.

I changed the RelVal part since the first version. As discussed, the RelVal logs are now scanned one step at a time in `parseLog`, just before `es_parse_log`. The hook I had in `process-relval-logs` is removed.

What changes:
- `runPyRelValThread.py`: a small call before `es_parse_log`, only for logs that are not in the cache yet.
- `es_ibs_log.py`: a small call after the unit test and addOn zips are unpacked.
- Two new files: `ib_test_log_problems.py` writes the results and `ib_test_log_scanner.py` finds the problems in the logs.

The results are small files (about 1 KB for a RelVal step) in `/data/sdt/chatbot-outbox`. The job in #2909 sends them to the chatbot and deletes them, so the folder is normally empty. If that job does not run for a day, the scan stops by itself and nothing piles up.

Every call is in a `try/except`, so a problem in our code only prints an error and your jobs continue as before.

It takes some extra time: about 2.5 minutes in total for a full RelVal build and about 12 minutes for the DBG unit tests, which are the biggest. DBG RelVals are skipped for now because their logs are very large (about 117 GB per run). We can look at them later in a separate job.

I tested it with the real scripts and the logs of CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-14-1100 (el9_amd64_gcc14), without sending anything to Elasticsearch. The results are the same as scanning the whole folder at once. I also tried it with our code missing or broken, and `parseLog` gave the same output as master.
title: Scan IB test logs for the IB chatbot while they are unpacked
